title: One-Pot In Situ Construction of a Highly Stable Acylhydrazone-Derived Dy Cluster with Photodynamic Sterilization Property

synthesis.procedure: A mixture of malonohydrazide (0.1 mmol, 13.21 mg), 4-(diethylamino)-2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (0.1 mmol, 19.32 mg), Dy(OAc)3·4H2O (0.4 mmol, approximately 165 mg), and triethylamine (100 μL) was dissolved in mixed solvent CH3OH/CH3CN/H2O (1.5:0.5:0.15 mL) in a Pyrex tube. The tube was sealed and heated at 80 °C in an oven for 3 days (72 h), affording yellow block crystals of cluster 1. Malonohydrazide and 4-(diethylamino)-2-hydroxybenzaldehyde undergo an in situ condensation to give H2L1.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: sealed Pyrex tube, solvothermal heating in an oven
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: yellow block crystals observed after heating; no additional workup described

properties.summary: Cluster 1 shows UV–vis ligand absorption at 380 nm and generates abundant ROS (1O2) under white-light irradiation via enhanced ISC from the Dy(III) heavy-atom/SOC effect, giving a TEMP–1O2 EPR signal and a 13.09-fold DCFH fluorescence increase in 40 s; photodynamic sterilization of S. aureus and E. coli is observed after 10 min Xe-lamp irradiation (inhibition zone up to 5.0 cm). Magnetically, χmT at 300 K is 127.17 cm3 K mol−1 (nine Dy(III)), falling to 88.70 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K; magnetization reaches 61.90 Nβ at 2 K and 7 T, hysteresis is not obvious at 2 K, and no clear frequency-dependent out-of-phase AC signal is seen under zero DC field.
